from itertools import combinations

# Verify using pysat
from pysat.solvers import Glucose3

n = 7
# Create edge list in lexicographic order
edges = [(i, j) for i in range(1, n+1) for j in range(i+1, n+1)]
print(f"Number of edges: {len(edges)}")
print(f"Edges: {edges}")

# Map edge to variable index (1-based)
edge_to_var = {e: idx+1 for idx, e in enumerate(edges)}

solver = Glucose3()

# For each triangle (i,j,k), add clauses:
# Not all red: at least one blue (at least one = 1)
# Not all blue: at least one red (at least one = 0)

triangles = [(i,j,k) for i in range(1,n+1) for j in range(i+1,n+1) for k in range(j+1,n+1)]
print(f"Number of triangles: {len(triangles)}")

for (i,j,k) in triangles:
    e1 = edge_to_var[(i,j)]
    e2 = edge_to_var[(i,k)]
    e3 = edge_to_var[(j,k)]
    
    # Not all red (not all 0): at least one must be 1 (blue)
    solver.add_clause([e1, e2, e3])
    
    # Not all blue (not all 1): at least one must be 0 (red), i.e., negation
    solver.add_clause([-e1, -e2, -e3])

result = solver.solve()
print(f"Satisfiable: {result}")

if result:
    model = solver.get_model()
    solution = []
    for e in edges:
        var = edge_to_var[e]
        solution.append(1 if var in model else 0)
    print(f"Solution: {solution}")
